subject.title: [security] Workspace SSH host private keys are persisted in cloud provider user-data

question: Does current `main` intentionally replace coordinator-generated workspace SSH host private keys with a guest-generated or otherwise non-retained trust bootstrap, and is that the supported permanent security boundary?
rationale: The vulnerable fields are absent from current source, but source inspection did not establish the replacement protocol, its authentication guarantees, or whether the change was intentional and release-ready.

options.title: Confirm the replacement design
options.body: Document the current host-identity bootstrap, identify its fixing commit, and add provider-level regression coverage before closing this issue.

options.title: Implement guest-generated identity
options.body: Generate the SSH host key inside the workspace and authenticate only its public identity back to the coordinator without provider-retained private material.

options.title: Retain coordinator generation securely
options.body: Deliver the private key through a non-retained authenticated channel and explicitly document the provider and coordinator trust assumptions.

recommendation.title: Confirm the replacement design
recommendation.body: Document the current host-identity bootstrap, identify its fixing commit, and add provider-level regression coverage before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history connects this contributor to central provider lifecycle and security-boundary work near the affected path.
